title: Perspectives and challenges in circularly polarized luminescence of lanthanide(III) complexes: From solution-based systems to solid-state applications
claim: CPL can be programmed into otherwise achiral Ln complexes or upconversion nanoparticles by embedding them in a chiral host—MOFs, helical gels, cellulose nanocrystals, or doped liquid crystals—whose photonic band gap or host–guest contacts set the handedness and can amplify glum.
explanation: Achiral [Ln(acac)3] in a camphorate Zn MOF, Eu-MOF-encapsulated halide perovskites, NaYF4:Yb/Er or Yb/Tm particles in chiral nanotubes or cellulose, and UCNPs in R/S811 liquid crystals all gain CPL without a chiral first coordination sphere on the emitter. Glycerol or dopant concentration tunes the photonic band gap and selectively amplifies bands; humidity can change both glum and host handedness. A dual band-edge overlap raised a UCNP NIR glum to about 0.5.
scope: Achiral molecular Ln complexes and lanthanide-doped upconversion nanoparticles assembled with chiral organic, MOF, or liquid-crystal media.
conditions: Upconversion examples use ~974–980 nm excitation. Photonic amplification requires the emission or excitation to overlap a band edge.
caveats: Host-induced glum values span orders of magnitude (about 10^-2 for the camphorate MOF guests versus ~0.5 in the optimized liquid crystal) and are not interchangeable. Adding a chiral matrix increases synthetic steps.
